instructions: For each fact, read only the quotes and their context. Verdict `support` when the quotes alone state every part of the claim and of each value, with the same scope and qualifiers; `partial` when a part is missing; `not-supported` when the quotes say something else; `unsure` otherwise. A quote with a `heading` is the value line under that heading on the page: read the two together. Do not use what you remember.

facts.claim: A resource share can have 5,000 resource associations (the default quota), and this quota is not adjustable.

evidence.title: Service quotas for AWS RAM
evidence.quote: | Maximum number of resource associations per resource share | 5,000 |
evidence.context:
| Resource | Default limit | 
| --- | --- | 
| Maximum number of resource shares per AWS Region | 25,000 | 
| Maximum number of resource associations per resource share | 5,000 | 
| Maximum number of principal associations per resource share | 5,000 | 
| Maximum number of customer managed permissions  | 1,500 | 
| Maximum number of customer managed permissions per resource type | 10 | 
| Maximum number of versions per customer managed permission | 5 | 
| Maximum number of resource associations across all resource shares in an AWS Region  Each resource included in a resource share counts against this limit. If a resource is included in 10 different resource shares, that counts 10 against the limit.  | 25,000 |

The quota for **Number of pending invitations** applies to only *sending* accounts who share with accounts that are ***not*** part of sender's AWS Organization.

facts.claim: Some resource types can't be shared with any account that isn't a member of the organization; the Shareable AWS resources page shows which resource types can be shared outside the organization.

values.display: Some resource types can’t be shared

evidence.title: Errors when trying to share with accounts outside of my organization
evidence.quote: Some resource types can’t be shared with any account that isn't a member of that organization. An example resource type with this restriction is virtual private connections (VPCs) that are part of Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2).
evidence.context: ### Some resource types can be shared only with accounts in the same organization Some resource types can’t be shared with any account that isn't a member of that organization. An example resource type with this restriction is virtual private connections (VPCs) that are part of Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2). To verify if you can share a particular resource type with accounts and principals outside of your organization, see [Shareable AWS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/shareable.html). ### The service-linked role wasn't successfully created
headings: Errors when trying to share with accounts outside of my organization

evidence.title: Errors when trying to share with accounts outside of my organization
evidence.quote: To verify if you can share a particular resource type with accounts and principals outside of your organization, see [Shareable AWS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/shareable.html).
evidence.context: ### Some resource types can be shared only with accounts in the same organization Some resource types can’t be shared with any account that isn't a member of that organization. An example resource type with this restriction is virtual private connections (VPCs) that are part of Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2). To verify if you can share a particular resource type with accounts and principals outside of your organization, see [Shareable AWS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/shareable.html). ### The service-linked role wasn't successfully created This issue can occur if the service-linked role `AWSServiceRoleForResourceAccessManager` wasn't successfully created when you turned on integration between AWS RAM and AWS Organizations.
